scenes.prompt: Commissioned editorial photography for Dwell magazine, modern-architecture spread; NOT a product render, NOT advertising, NOT stock. Hasselblad X2D 100C, 45mm f/2.8 lens, aperture f/4. Exterior concrete staircase of a California hillside residence, photographed at dusk. The KOMILT 035 solar step light is surface-mounted flush on the riser of the third step, ankle-level, emitting a contained warm-white glow that pools only on the tread above it — it is a small integrated element, not the visual focus. The concrete risers show hairline shrinkage cracks, a faint efflorescence bloom near the base, and a dust film across the upper treads. Exposure is committed: the sky above clips to pale grey, the lower steps fall into genuine shadow with no fill. Zero color cast — the warm LED stays local to the riser face, the ambient dusk reads as neutral blue-grey. Kodak Portra 400 grain throughout, 2% corner vignette, 1px chromatic aberration at the brightest LED edge. Palette: raw concrete grey, oxidised steel handrail, warm ivory LED spill, dry-grass amber, deep charcoal shadow. No people, no alcohol. The fixture matches the variant reference image exactly — finish and form as shown.
scenes.cameraAngle: low three-quarter, shooting up the stair run
